newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai in $400 mln Indonesia car JV.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai in $400 mln Indonesia car JV.

text.p: South Korea's largest carmaker Hyundai Motor Co said on Thursday it had agreed with Indonesian conglomerate Bimantara Citra on a $400 million joint venture to make sedans in the southeast Asian country.
A spokesman for the flagship unit of Hyundai Group said each side would hold a 50 percent stake in the joint venture's paid-in capital of $150 million.
He said total investment would be $400 million in the project to make 50,000 units based on Hyundai's Avante model from mid-1999 at a plant to be built near Jakarta.
"We have agreed on the deal but the official contract will be signed once we get government approval," he said.
The Indonesian conglomerate, controlled by President Suharto's second son Bambang Trihatmodjo, has already been assembling cars with kits supplied by Hyundai, he said.
